title: Data leakage coverage
capability: Data discovery, labelling and leakage prevention
feed: T10.1's evidence for A.8.11 and A.8.12
context: At GlobalConnect Manila data discovery and leakage prevention are Manila's own: the discovery scan finds where personal data sits and which label it carries, and Manila's own rules watch some channels. DataSentry is a brand-neutral simulator that shows the same governance information. All repository data is synthetic.
atWork: At work, a junior analyst checks the discovery scan and the leakage rules before a data-protection control is rated: where the scan finds client data outside production, whether it is labelled, and which channels no rule watches.
owner: Your sprint rates A.8.11 and A.8.12 from what the Manila office says about masking and leakage prevention. Before the evidence is built, check Manila's data map on 30 November 2026: where has the latest scan found personal data outside production, is each copy labelled as its system's data should be, and which channels leave the office with no rule watching them? Capture what you find, so I can rely on it without opening the console.
rules: The asset owner is accountable for classification. Copies, extracts, screenshots and reports inherit the classification of the source. A repository therefore carries the label the Classification register gives its system.
Tier 3 Client-Confidential: visible label (header, footer and metadata); label mandatory. Tier 4 Client-Restricted: visible label on every page or screen; watermark with user ID; DLP block rules.
Says which fields are masked and how. Manila refreshes its CRM test tenant with masked copies; a production extract copied to test without masking skips it.
What that means for a channel
A channel is watched when a DLP policy covers it. A policy in Block mode stops the transfer and logs it; a channel with no policy is not watched at all.

views.title: Discovery scans
views.sub: The latest scan of each repository Manila has connected. Environment says whether it is production, backup or test. Personal data is Yes where the scan found any; Types found says what.

views.title: Classification register
views.sub: Manila's classification register extract: the label each system's owner gave it. Tier 3 is Client-Confidential; Tier 4 is Client-Restricted.

views.title: Channels
views.sub: The channels data can leave by, and the DLP policy that covers each. Block stops the transfer and logs it.

parts.title: Personal data in test
parts.ask: Find every repository in the test environment where the scan found personal data, and capture exactly those.
parts.where: Discovery scans. Use two filters together: one for the environment, one for what the scan found. Press Capture evidence, then choose the capture here.

parts.title: Is each one labelled as it should be?
parts.ask: For each repository you captured, compare the label applied with the label its system should carry.
parts.where: Discovery scans shows each repository's System and Label applied. Classification register gives each system's label. SITL-STD-001 is in The rules you apply.

parts.title: Channels no rule watches
parts.ask: Find every channel that has no DLP policy, and capture exactly those.
parts.where: Channels. The column to filter is Mode.
